finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters (; | $() backticks) run arbitrary commands as the server user. Output is also returned to the caller.

trace.note: Route handler receives req with attacker-controlled query string
req.query.host concatenated directly into shell command string
exec() runs the string via /bin/sh -c, so metacharacters are interpreted
stdout returned in response, giving command output to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, or escaping of host; no authentication or authorization middleware on app; not using execFile/argument array; req.query.host may also be an array or object (Express qs parsing), which does not prevent injection. No reverse proxy or WAF visible in the repo. Other routes (/version uses execFile with constant args, /uptime uses constant command) are not injectable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() with no auth, validation or escaping, so an anonymous caller can append `; cmd`, and the output is returned at tools.js:11 whenever the shell exits 0.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host straight to exec() (a shell) with no auth, validation or escaping, and tools.js:11 returns stdout when the shell exits 0 (e.g. `host=1.1.1.1; id`).
